front.title: Signed Public Certificate Bundles for Hardware-Backed Messaging Identities

abstract.t: This document describes a signed, compressed public certificate bundle used to restore hardware-backed messaging identities on another computer. A bundle carries S/MIME certificates, OpenPGP certificates, and bindings between public keys and device key references. A single-bank storage binding uses application data objects in a YubiKey PIV application, with a verified local recovery copy made before replacement. Private keys and authentication credentials are excluded. The document specifies the deployed base payload and proposes a separately versioned extension payload for additional certificate types and explicit component-to-slot mappings. It is intended for the Independent Submission Stream as an Informational document.

note.title: Discussion and implementation status
note.t: This is a working draft, not an IETF consensus specification. Publication in a source repository does not constitute submission to the Internet-Draft repository or acceptance by the Independent Submissions Editor. Discussion and source: . The compressed single-bank base format has been tested with PQ Mail and a separate Sequoia-based reader. The extension payload in this document is a proposal; deployed readers do not yet accept it. Only the current single-bank storage arrangement is specified. Historical encodings and storage arrangements are out of scope.

section.name: Introduction and Scope
section.t: A hardware token can hold private keys without holding enough public identity information for a new messaging client to use them. In particular, one OpenPGP composite key may involve two hardware slots, and an application may offer both pure post-quantum and composite S/MIME certificates over shared components. A public certificate bundle preserves certificates, their signatures, and their hardware bindings without exporting private keys.

Backup means writing public identity information to the device. Restore means reading that information and creating local references to existing device keys. Neither operation generates, imports, moves, or deletes a private key. Restore does not issue certificates and MUST NOT automatically grant contact trust.

The device binding described here is application-specific. Its object identifiers are not allocations from the PIV standard. Other smart cards require a separately documented storage binding, sufficient storage, suitable key operations, and a means of retrieving or verifying public keys. Having a PKCS#11 interface alone does not satisfy those requirements. The format does not require a particular private-operation API.

section.name: Conventions and Terminology
section.t: The key words MUST, MUST NOT, REQUIRED, SHALL, SHALL NOT, SHOULD, SHOULD NOT, RECOMMENDED, NOT RECOMMENDED, MAY, and OPTIONAL in this document are to be interpreted as described in BCP 14 when, and only when, they appear in all capitals.

A profile pairs a signing certificate with an encryption certificate and optional OpenPGP material. A component is one constituent public key of a composite key. A slot is a PIV key reference, not a data-object identifier. A bank is the one manifest and its numbered data chunks. A binding identifies which existing device key implements a certificate key or component. Certificate validity, bundle integrity, live key matching, and correspondent trust are distinct results.

section.name: Encoding Layers and Limits
section.artwork: PIV data objects manifest + numbered chunks PQMZIP01: zlib-compressed signed envelope PQMAILS1: payload + signer index + signature PQMAILB2: deployed base profiles PQMAILB3: proposed base profiles + extensions
section.t: All integers are unsigned, big-endian octet sequences. U8, U32, and U64 occupy one, four, and eight octets respectively. To match current implementations, a device serial is in 1..2147483647 and a generation is in 1..9223372036854775807. Lengths and counts MUST be checked before allocation, addition, multiplication, or slicing. Implementations MUST reject overflow, truncation, inconsistent counts, and trailing bytes at every defined layer.
section.artwork: BLOB(x) = U32(length(x)) || x || = octet concatenation MAGIC = exactly eight ASCII octets, without a terminator
section.t: The compressed object stream and the decompressed signed envelope MUST each be at most 65536 octets. A BLOB MUST fit within its enclosing structure and this limit. Zero-length BLOBs are allowed only where stated. A base profile count is 2..16, including at least one pure and one composite profile. These bounds are protocol limits, not a promise that a device has enough free storage. Writers MUST account for object overhead and other applications sharing device storage.

section.name: Compressed Container
section.t: The stream is one zlib stream containing a DEFLATE representation of the complete signed envelope. It is not a ZIP archive, gzip member, raw DEFLATE stream, or OpenPGP Compressed Data packet. A preset dictionary MUST NOT be used. Compression level is not fixed, so compressed bytes need not be reproducible.

The expanded length MUST be 1..65536 and MUST equal the actual output length. Readers MUST stop expansion at the declared bound, require end of stream and the zlib checksum, and reject additional output, concatenated streams, trailing compressed input, and dictionary requests. No decompressed data is trusted before envelope verification. An implementation SHOULD also bound CPU time.

section.name: Signed Envelope
section.t: The signer index is zero-based and selects a base profile's signing certificate. The signature covers the exact payload octets, including its magic and all lengths. It does not cover the envelope magic, signer index, compression, generation, or manifest. Verifiers MUST select the indicated key, determine the permitted signature algorithm from its SubjectPublicKeyInfo (SPKI), and verify the supplied signature over the original payload bytes. Re-serialization before verification is prohibited.

The certificate issuer's signature algorithm is not the bundle signing algorithm. Pure ML-DSA uses the matching pure algorithm with an empty application context, not HashML-DSA. Composite signatures use the algorithm identified by the SPKI, including its prescribed hashing, domain separation, component ordering, and signature encoding. Implementations MUST verify every component. The bundle adds no separate signature context. Passing a precomputed external mu to hardware is an implementation detail and MUST produce the same signature semantics.

Writers SHOULD use the composite signing profile. Readers MAY require that profile by local policy, but MUST NOT silently accept only its classical component. Since the signer index is outside the signature, its integrity is conditional on successful verification with the selected key; it is not independently authenticated metadata.

section.name: Deployed Base Payload
section.artwork:
base_payload = "PQMAILB2" || U32(profile_count) || profile[profile_count]
profile = U32(device_serial) || U8(pq_sign_slot) || U8(classical_sign_slot) || U8(pq_decrypt_slot) || U8(classical_decrypt_slot) || BLOB(signing_certificate_der) || BLOB(encryption_certificate_der) || BLOB(openpgp_public_certificate) || BLOB(openpgp_v4_compatibility_certificate)
section.t: The X.509 BLOBs are nonempty and each contains exactly one DER certificate . They are not PEM, CMS SignedData, certificate chains, or private-key containers. The OpenPGP BLOBs contain binary public certificate packets, not ASCII armor or secret-key packets. Either OpenPGP field MAY be empty; a nonempty compatibility field requires a nonempty public certificate field. All original certificate packets, including certification and binding signatures, MUST be preserved.

All profiles MUST name the same device serial and the same four distinct slots. Pure and composite profiles MUST share the same ML-DSA and ML-KEM public components. A given slot MUST NOT be bound to different public keys anywhere in the payload. Duplicate signing/encryption certificate pairs are invalid. The current base profile places ML-DSA signing in 9c; the current creation layout uses 83, 9d, and 82 for the remaining fields in that order. PIV references are encoded as single octets, for example hexadecimal 83 is the octet 0x83, not the ASCII string "83".

Legal ordinary PIV references for base fields are 9a, 9c, 9d, 9e, and 82 through 95, hexadecimal. This range is syntax validation only: the four current role assignments and supported algorithm profile still have to match. Attestation and PIN/PUK references MUST NOT be treated as application keys. Importers MUST NOT move keys to satisfy a mapping.

section.name: S/MIME Algorithm Profiles
section.t: Each base profile uses one row of the following table, with the corresponding pure or composite form for both signing and encryption. The OID suffixes in the last two columns are relative to 1.3.6.1.5.5.7.6. Level labels describe the ML-DSA category, not a certification of the complete system. In particular, ML-KEM-768 is category 3 in both the Level 2 and Level 3 profiles.

Pure ML-DSA SPKI OIDs are 2.16.840.1.101.3.4.3.17, .18, and .19 respectively; ML-KEM-768 and ML-KEM-1024 SPKI OIDs are 2.16.840.1.101.3.4.4.2 and .3. Their AlgorithmIdentifier parameters are absent. Composite identifiers and encodings follow the corresponding algorithm specifications . These identifier assignments are used, not allocated, by this document. Implementations MUST NOT equate similarly named experimental algorithms having different identifiers or encodings.

The first composite component maps to the PQ slot, and the second to the classical slot. Pure profiles map only their single component; the companion composite profile supplies the classical public keys. Readers MUST parse the algorithm's actual component encoding rather than treating the composite SPKI as a single device key.

Signing and encryption certificates MUST share at least one rfc822Name SAN mailbox. For activation as a messaging identity, validity periods and applicable KeyUsage and ExtendedKeyUsage restrictions MUST be checked; emailProtection or anyExtendedKeyUsage is required when an EKU restriction is present. Signing uses digitalSignature; the base ML-KEM/composite KEM profiles use keyEncipherment. Parsing a backup for inspection does not itself authorize use of expired or revoked credentials. CA path building and revocation policy remain the application's responsibility.

section.name: OpenPGP Content and Base Slot Bindings
section.t: OpenPGP certificates follow and supported algorithm profiles such as . Readers MUST validate self-certifications, subkey bindings, required signing-subkey back-signatures, key flags, and revocation/expiration policy before activating a key. A packet's presence alone does not authorize its use. Secret-Key and Secret-Subkey packets MUST be rejected. Unrecognized algorithms MUST NOT be guessed from lengths or replaced with classical operations.

For the currently tested Level 3 separated-certification profile, the base format uses the following fixed additional mappings. They are not additional fields in PQMAILB2. A reader MUST recognize this complete profile and match every public component before activating it, or report the profile as unsupported. The same logical public key may occur in more than one certificate view without implying another device key.

tr.td: v6 classical signing subkey / v4 primary

section.t: The v4 view uses the appropriate v4 packet encodings for its classical keys. A v6 certificate and a v4 certificate have different primary keys and fingerprints; correspondence MUST be verified by their certified identities and constituent public keys, not by assuming their fingerprints match. Unsupported OpenPGP profiles can be retained as opaque public backup data but MUST NOT become usable hardware identities.

A classical-only v4 view MAY be obtained by retaining the original primary key, User IDs and their certifications, and the classical encryption subkey with its existing binding signatures and relevant revocations, while omitting the hybrid encryption subkey and signatures pertaining to it. No signature is created and no PIN is needed. The primary-key fingerprint stays unchanged. Filtering MUST NOT remove a revocation or restriction applicable to a retained key, invent a binding, or silently change the selected cryptographic policy. The resulting view MUST be verified again.

section.name: Proposed Extension Payload
section.t: This section defines a proposed, separately versioned payload. It is not implemented by the deployed PQMAILB2 readers. A writer MUST NOT use it for an installation that has not explicitly enabled extension support. The single-bank storage, compression, and signed-envelope formats are unchanged. Unknown payload magic MUST cause a clear unsupported-format error; a reader MUST NOT strip extensions to try base verification.
section.artwork:
extended_payload = "PQMAILB3" || U32(profile_count) || profile[profile_count] || U32(extension_count) || extension[extension_count]
extension = BLOB(type_identifier) || U8(flags) || BLOB(value)
section.t: The profile encoding is exactly that in . Extension count is 0..32. Type identifiers are 1..192 ASCII octets containing an absolute HTTPS URI under the defining party's control. They are compared byte-for-byte, are unique within a payload, and MUST NOT be fetched or used as executable locations. Bit 0 of flags means critical; all other bits MUST be zero. Unknown critical extensions cause rejection of the entire payload. Unknown noncritical extensions MUST NOT affect usable identity, key selection, trust, or device commands. A reader MAY retain them as opaque signed bytes. A writer rewriting an imported bundle MUST preserve them or explicitly refuse the rewrite; silent loss is prohibited.

All extensions are covered by the envelope signature. Extensions MUST NOT override a base certificate, change its mapping, grant trust, designate an executable, supply credentials, or request provisioning. Conflicts cause rejection. The extension mechanism is additive: existing base S/MIME profiles remain required and continue to identify the envelope signer.

section.name: Additional Certificate Set
section.t: The type identifier is https://github.com/ve7jtb/pq-mail/spec/certificate-set/v1. The value is:
section.artwork:
U32(certificate_count) || certificate_record[certificate_count]
certificate_record = U32(certificate_id) || BLOB(format_identifier) || U32(purposes) || BLOB(certificate)
section.t: Count is 1..32. IDs are nonzero and unique within this set. Purposes is a bit mask: bit 0 signing, bit 1 decryption, bit 2 certification, bit 3 issuer-chain support. At least one bit MUST be set, other bits MUST be zero, and issuer-chain support MUST NOT be combined with other purposes. Purposes request local use and MUST NOT expand permissions in the certificate itself. Certificates are nonempty and public-only.

Format identifiers are 1..192 ASCII octets. This version defines the exact identifiers "x509-der" for one DER X.509 certificate and "openpgp-public" for one binary OpenPGP public certificate. Other formats use an absolute HTTPS URI and MUST define public-only syntax, key identification, signature validation, permitted uses, and component extraction. Unknown formats in a critical certificate set cause rejection. In a noncritical set they MAY be retained only as opaque data and MUST NOT be activated.

This extension can carry additional S/MIME signing/encryption certificates or issuer certificates without replacing the base pair. Issuer-chain certificates have no private-slot mapping and do not become trust anchors. The application still needs its ordinary S/MIME chain, identity, validity, key-usage, and revocation checks. A noncritical certificate set is suitable only for information that may safely be ignored.

section.name: Explicit Public-Key Mappings
section.t: The type identifier is https://github.com/ve7jtb/pq-mail/spec/key-mappings/v1. This extension MUST be critical, and its value is:
section.artwork:
U32(binding_count) || binding[binding_count]
binding = U32(certificate_id) || BLOB(key_selector) || U32(component_index) || U32(roles) || BLOB(locator_type) || BLOB(locator) || BLOB(component_spki_der)
section.t: Count is 1..64. Each certificate ID MUST refer to the certificate-set extension. For X.509, key_selector is empty and selects the subject public key. For OpenPGP it is the full binary fingerprint of the selected primary key or subkey, of the length defined for that key version; short key IDs are forbidden. A component index is zero-based in the order defined by the certificate algorithm; a noncomposite key has only index 0. It MUST NOT be inferred from field lengths. For example, OpenPGP wire order and an X.509 composite algorithm's order need not agree.

Roles uses bits 0 signing, 1 decryption, and 2 certification, with at least one bit set and no other bits. Roles MUST be a subset of the referenced certificate's requested purposes and its authenticated key flags/usages. A tuple (certificate_id, key_selector, component_index) MUST appear once only; several permitted roles are combined in that tuple. Every component of every key being activated MUST have a binding. No omitted component may be silently downgraded or synthesized.

The SPKI is the canonical DER encoding of the individual component, with the algorithm and parameters appropriate to that component. Readers MUST derive it from the referenced certificate key and compare it with both the supplied SPKI and the live device key. All bindings naming the same locator MUST agree on the public key. A binding that overlaps a base or fixed-profile mapping MUST agree with it exactly.

This version defines locator_type "piv-key-reference". Its locator is exactly one octet identifying an ordinary key slot on the same device serial as the base profiles. Other locator types use an absolute HTTPS URI and need a separate specification of device identification, key addressing, and safe public-key matching. An unsupported locator makes the critical extension unsupported. A locator MUST NOT contain a PIN, management key, executable path, PKCS#11 module path, arbitrary command, or remote callback URL.

These mappings permit additional S/MIME certificates, multiple OpenPGP keys, and other specified certificate formats without assuming particular PIV slots. They do not enable a device algorithm, change touch/PIN policy, or prove a private key is nonexportable. Import MUST show the proposed mappings for user review.

section.name: Single-Bank PIV Storage Binding
section.t: The YubiKey PIV application documents application-defined GET DATA and PUT DATA objects . This binding uses object 0x5f5000 for the manifest and objects 0x5f5001 through 0x5f5020 for up to 32 chunks. These are application conventions, not globally reserved tags. Writers MUST detect namespace collisions and MUST NOT overwrite unrelated or unrecognized data. Standard PIV certificate objects are not used for the bundle.

Object values below exclude APDU framing, status words, and PIV data-object TLV wrappers. A transport adapter MUST remove only those wrappers, assemble ISO 7816 response chaining correctly, and supply exact object bytes. USB and NFC must yield identical bytes. Only an explicit object-not-found result is absence; permission failures, tag loss, timeouts, malformed responses, and transport errors MUST remain errors.
section.artwork:
manifest (52 octets): "PQMIDX01" || U64(generation) || U32(stored_length) || SHA256(compressed)
chunk i at object 0x5f5001 + i: "PQMCHK01" || U64(generation) || U32(i) || chunk_data
section.t: Stored length is 1..65536. The number of chunks is ceiling(stored_length / 2048), at most 32. Index i starts at zero. Every chunk except the last carries exactly 2048 data octets; the last carries precisely the remaining 1..2048 octets. All chunk generations MUST equal the manifest generation. The digest covers the concatenated compressed data, not the chunk headers. Its purpose is complete-object consistency checking, not authentication or rollback protection.

A successful write retains only this bank. No second on-card recovery copy is required or written. Unused tail chunk objects SHOULD be removed after local backup, subject to namespace ownership checks. Hardware keys, ordinary PIV certificate objects, PIN/PUK values, touch policies, and other applications MUST remain unchanged.

section.name: Read and Restore

ol.li: Read the manifest; reject invalid sizes or generations. Obtain each required chunk and require exact header and data lengths.
Concatenate data and verify the manifest digest. Re-read the manifest and require it to be byte-identical, or report concurrent modification.
Perform bounded decompression and parse the complete envelope and payload. Reject unsupported critical features and inconsistent mappings.
Verify the envelope signature and the certificate-specific bindings. Check all required live public keys and the device serial before offering hardware identity activation.

Show mailbox identities, full fingerprints, algorithms, device identifier, and slot mappings for review. Import public-only identities after confirmation; do not import trust, credentials, or executable settings.

section.t: Reading from a file can verify signatures without a card, but the result MUST be labeled not yet matched to hardware. A missing required key or a mismatch blocks hardware activation. Serial numbers are routing hints, not cryptographic device authentication. Public-key matching does not prove hardware provenance or private-key possession; those require separate attestation or an explicitly authorized private operation.

section.name: Replacement and Local Recovery

ol.li: Construct and validate the replacement payload, check device identity and every required public key, authorize bundle signing, and verify the resulting signature locally. Produce the compressed representation within the size bounds.
Snapshot every existing object in the owned bank. Refuse unrelated data or ambiguous ownership. If a complete prior bundle exists, verify and retain it as well.

Before any card mutation, save the original object bytes, verified prior envelope if available, replacement signed envelope, and replacement compressed bytes to a new local recovery directory. Include lengths and SHA-256 digests. Flush files, make directory entries durable where the platform permits, read the files back, and revalidate the replacement. If this cannot be completed, stop without card writes.

Obtain management authorization locally. Recheck the complete object snapshot, including absence of previously absent objects, and device identity before destructive work. Serialize access where supported; if the state has changed, stop and replan.

Delete or invalidate the manifest first, then remove the owned old chunks to release space. Do not treat a failed delete as success. Write each replacement chunk and verify its exact bytes by read-back.

Write the manifest last. Read the complete bank through the normal verification path, compare it with the intended replacement, and check live keys again. Record local completion only after success. Retain the local recovery copy.

section.t: There is deliberately no atomic availability guarantee during overwrite: removal, interruption, or storage failure can leave no valid on-card bundle. The UI MUST disclose this before backup. Automatic blind retries of a partially completed mutation are prohibited. An explicit recovery operation MUST inspect current device state and the saved recovery files, recheck keys, and obtain any required management authorization before rewriting. It MUST NOT regenerate keys or change touch/PIN policies.

The generation increments after a valid previous generation; the initial generation is 1. Writers MUST reject overflow. A resumed write without a valid manifest uses the generation saved in the recovery transaction. Generations are unauthenticated operational counters, not secure monotonic counters. An old valid signed bundle can be replayed; freshness needs separate trusted local state or an explicitly confirmed comparison.

Suggested recovery names are previous.pqkey, replacement.pqkey, replacement.pqmzip, object-TAG.bin, recovery.txt, and complete.txt. These names are local conventions, not wire fields. Directory permissions SHOULD limit disclosure of personal identity information. Files MUST NOT contain PINs, private keys, OAuth tokens, management secrets, or trusted-contact decisions. Recovery data MUST NOT be automatically published.

section.name: Security Considerations
section.t: A bundle is public, not confidential. Anyone able to read its objects may learn mailbox addresses, device identifiers, certificate relationships, and key fingerprints. Compression does not conceal this information. Shared copies and local recovery files warrant the same privacy treatment as the certificates themselves.

A signature made by a key contained in the same bundle proves consistency with that key, not the owner's real-world identity. An attacker can create an entirely self-consistent replacement using the attacker's own keys. Live public-key checks and independently established correspondent trust are separate requirements. Restore MUST NOT automatically mark any mailbox/fingerprint pair trusted or turn included CA certificates into roots.

Bundles MUST contain only public material and declarative mappings. Implementations MUST reject private-key packets and prevent path traversal, executable configuration, automatic URL fetching, and command construction from certificate or extension data. Displayed identity strings require escaping and length limits. Import must stage all validation before persistent activation; failures MUST NOT leave partially trusted identities.

Signature-valid certificates can be expired, revoked, or unsuitable for the requested purpose. Removing a hybrid subkey can yield a still-valid classical certificate view. Therefore signature validity alone does not promise hybrid capabilities or authorize a downgrade. Applications MUST disclose classical fallback separately for signing and encryption and apply their local acceptance policy.

Storage ownership cannot be established by magic bytes alone. Before deleting, the writer must inspect the namespace and its application context; unexpected objects require explicit recovery review. The local recovery mechanism protects availability only to the extent the backup was durably saved and remains accessible. The unauthenticated manifest and generation permit denial of service and rollback. No claim of transactionality across power loss is made.

Readers MUST bound decompression, parsing, certificate counts, packet nesting, and signature work. Failed hardware reads MUST NOT be converted to missing objects or empty slots. A restore operation requires no signing PIN or private operation in this storage binding. An application MUST NOT retry a PIN after rejection or modify key policy to complete restore.

section.name: IANA Considerations
section.t: This document requests no IANA actions. The PIV object tags and extension identifiers are application-specific conventions and do not reserve a PIV namespace, an IANA registry, an OID, a URI scheme, or a media type. Existing cryptographic identifiers retain their specifications. The local file suffixes .pqkey and .pqmzip do not establish registered MIME types.

section.name: Implementation and Interoperability Status
section.t: As of 20 November 2026, a Level 3 bundle using the deployed base payload was written to a single bank on a PQC Ready YubiKey Beta0, restored into a fresh PQ Mail store, and independently read and verified with a Sequoia-based adapter. The tests compared public keys and PIN/touch policies before and after. This establishes interoperability for that tested profile, not universal hardware support or a production security audit.

The companion public software fixture uses synthetic identities and a synthetic serial; no private keys or actual user's hardware backup are included. It exercises pure and composite envelope signatures, compressed framing, and separated certification/signing keys. The extension payload, other-card bindings, and all possible certificate algorithms require additional implementation and interoperability testing.

section.name: Companion Test Material
section.t: The repository accompanying this draft includes a public-only software fixture, a framing validator, and build instructions. The fixture contains both pure-signed and composite-signed compressed base bundles and the expected component SPKIs. It MUST NOT be used as a production identity. The framing validator does not replace cryptographic signature verification; independent signature validation uses the Sequoia adapter test suite.

Negative tests should include truncated chunks, wrong indices/generations, digest mismatch, invalid zlib boundaries, expansion overflow, trailing bytes, invalid signatures in either composite component, secret OpenPGP packets, invalid bindings, wrong device or key, conflicting mappings, unknown critical extensions, namespace collisions, and interruption after every mutation step. A successful reader must not perform a private-key operation or confer contact trust.
